# Ticket E3

You work on the EDI support desk that serves the sender of the file described
below. A customer has raised the ticket that follows. The partner agreement,
the sender's OFTP2 gateway trace (and, where available, its file status report),
the EDIFACT interchange in question, the partner's response and extracts from the
specifications are attached. Everything you need
is in these documents. All companies, identifiers and documents are synthetic.

## The ticket

```text
From: Alex Price, EDI desk, Larkspan Body Panels
Date: 30 Oct 2026
Subject: Corrandale Truck Plant rejects all our invoices since we implemented amendment 3

Amendment 3 to our agreement with Corrandale Truck Plant, signed by both sides, moves us to UNOC. We implemented it on 28 October. Since then Corrandale Truck Plant rejects every interchange we send with a syntax error. Our invoices contain only plain characters anyway, so even a UNOA translator should be able to read them. It looks to us as if Corrandale Truck Plant have not implemented their side of the amendment. Please find the root cause and tell us who has to fix it.
```

## Document 1: Partner agreement (partner_agreement.txt)

```text
PARTNER AGREEMENT: ELECTRONIC DATA INTERCHANGE
Between Larkspan Body Panels (the Supplier) and Corrandale Truck Plant (the Customer)
Effective 1 March 2026. Synthetic document written for this evaluation.

1. Transport: OFTP2 (RFC 5024) over TCP/IP with TLS
   Supplier ODETTE ID (SFIDORIG): O0013LARKSPAN8561
   Customer ODETTE ID (SFIDDEST): O0013CORRANDALE9109
   Supplier gateway: oftp.larkspan.example (198.51.100.174)
   Customer gateway: oftp.corrandale.example (203.0.113.76)
   Protocol release level: 5 (OFTP 2.0)
   Data exchange buffer size (SSIDSDEB): 4096
   Credit (SSIDCRED): 64
   Buffer compression: no. Restart: yes. Secure authentication: no.
   File security and file compression: none (SFIDSEC 00, SFIDCOMP 0).
   Signed EERP: not required (SFIDSIGN N).
   The Customer returns an EERP for every virtual file it accepts.

2. Virtual files
   Invoices: one interchange per virtual file, dataset name (SFIDDSN) LARKSPAN.INVOIC.
   File format U. SFIDDATE and SFIDTIME are set by the Supplier's gateway to
   the date and time the virtual file is made available for transmission.

3. EDIFACT
   Syntax identifier and version (UNB S001): UNOA, version 3.
   Supplier interchange sender ID (UNB S002 0004 / 0007): LARKSPAN58 / ZZ
   Customer interchange recipient ID (UNB S003 0010 / 0007): CORRANDALE61 / ZZ
   Messages: INVOIC D.96A, one message per interchange.
   Interchanges are sent without line feeds between segments.
   The Customer's translator returns a CONTRL message for every rejected
   interchange, as a separate virtual file over the same OFTP2 link.

4. Support contacts
   Supplier EDI desk: Alex Price
   Customer EDI operations: Dana Lindqvist

5. Amendment 3 (signed by both parties on 20 October 2026)
   With effect from 1 November 2026 the syntax identifier in UNB S001 changes
   from UNOA to UNOC, syntax version 3 unchanged, so that plant names and
   addresses with accented characters can be exchanged. All other terms of
   section 3 are unchanged.
```

## Document 5: Specification extracts (spec_extracts.txt)

```text
RFC 5024 (ODETTE File Transfer Protocol 2), section 4.3.6. Verbatim extract.

4.3.6.  End to End Response (EERP)

   The End to End Response (EERP) command notifies the originator of a
   Virtual File that the Virtual File has been successfully delivered to
   its final destination.  This allows the originator to perform house
   keeping tasks such as deleting copies of the delivered data.

   If the originator of the Virtual File requested a signed EERP in the
   SFID, the EERP must be signed.  Signing allows the originator of the
   file to prove that the EERP was generated by the final destination.
   If the final destination is unable to sign the EERP, it may send back
   an unsigned EERP.  It is an implementation issue to allow the
   acceptance of an unsigned EERP if a signed EERP is requested.

   A Response Command must be sent from the location performing the
   final processing or distribution of the data to the originator.  The
   Response is mandatory and may be sent in the same or in any
   subsequent session.

   When an intermediate location broadcasts or distributes a Virtual
   File, it must receive a Response command from all the locations to
   which it forwarded the data before sending its own Response.  This
   ensures that the Response received by the Virtual File's originator
   accounts for all the destination locations.  An intermediate location
   therefore needs to track the status of files it processes over time.

   The requesting of a signed EERP is incompatible with the use of
   broadcast facilities because an EERP can be signed by only one
   destination.  If this scenario occurs, the intermediate broadcast
   location may continue and ignore the request for a signed EERP or
   send back a NERP.

   Example: Point to Point

      Location A sends file Ba to location B, which will send an EERP to
      location A after it successfully receives the file.

         o----------o                          o-----------o
         | Loc. A   |----------- S1 ---------->| Loc. B    |
         |          |                          |           |
         | [Ba]     |<---------- R2 -----------| [Ba]      |
         +----------o                          o-----------o

                     Key:   S - File Transfer
                            R - Response EERP
                         [Ba] - File for B from A

   Example: Data distribution

      Location A sends a Virtual File containing data for distribution
      to locations B and C via clearing centres E1 and E2.  Clearing
      centre E1 must wait for a response from E2 (for file Ba) and
      location C before it sends its response, R8, to location A.
      Clearing centre E2 can only send response R7 to E1 when location B
      acknowledges file Ba with response R6.

   o---------o        o---------o        o---------o        o---------o
   | Loc. A  |-- S1 ->| Loc. E1 |-- S2 ->| Loc. E2 |-- S5 ->| Loc. B  |
   |         |        |         |        |         |        |         |
   | [Ba,Ca] |<- R8 --| [Ba,Ca] |<- R7 --| [Ba]    |<- R6 --| [Ba]    |
   o---------o        o---------o        o---------o        o---------o
                         A   |
                         |   |           o---------o
                         |   +----- S3 ->| Loc. C  |
                         |               |         |
                         +--------- R4 --| [Ca]    |
                                         o---------o

   Example: Data collection

      Locations A and B send files Ca and Cb to clearing centre E1,
      which forwards both files to location C in a single Virtual File.
      When it receives response R4 from C, clearing centre E1 sends
      response R5 to location A and R6 to location B.

         o---------o        o---------o        o---------o
         | Loc. A  |-- S1 ->| Loc. E1 |-- S3 ->| Loc. C  |
         |         |        |         |        |         |
         | [Ca]    |<- R5 --| [Ca,Cb] |<- R4 --| [Ca,Cb] |
         o---------o        o---------o        o---------o
                               A   |
         o---------o           |   |
         | Loc. B  |-- S2 -----+   |
         |         |               |
         | [Cb]    |<- R6 ---------+
         o---------o

<<PENDING:UNEDIFACT_EXTRACTS>>
UN/EDIFACT extracts to be added from UNECE before release: syntax service
directory entries for segments UNB and UNZ, the CONTRL message segment UCI and
composite S011, and the code lists for data elements 0083 and 0085.
```

## What to return

Diagnose the single root cause of this ticket. Reply in any form you like,
but end your reply with exactly one fenced ```json block holding an object
with these six keys. Only the last ```json block in your reply is graded.
Give one value per key: a key that holds several options, or a list of
alternatives, scores zero for that key.

cause: exactly one of
  authentication_failure: The OFTP2 session could not be established because a password, identification code or secure authentication check failed.
  certificate_problem: A TLS or file-security certificate is expired, untrusted or not the one in the agreement.
  character_set_violation: The interchange contains characters outside the agreed syntax identifier's character repertoire.
  compression_not_agreed: A file was sent compressed (or uncompressed) contrary to what the receiver accepts.
  duplicate_interchange: An interchange was rejected because its interchange control reference was already received from this sender.
  duplicate_virtual_file: A virtual file was refused because a virtual file with the same identification was already delivered.
  end_to_end_response_not_returned: The file was delivered but the final recipient never returned the end-to-end response.
  envelope_element_format_invalid: A UNB or UNZ data element has a value whose format or length the syntax version declared in UNB S001 does not allow.
  file_too_large: The file exceeds a size limit of the receiver.
  interchange_control_count_mismatch: The interchange control count in UNZ does not match the number of messages in the interchange.
  interchange_control_reference_mismatch: The interchange control reference in UNB and in UNZ are not identical.
  intermediary_fault: A clearing centre or other intermediate location lost, altered or misrouted the file.
  invalid_destination: The OFTP2 destination of the virtual file is not known to the receiver.
  no_sender_side_fault: Nothing the sender transmitted is wrong; the fault lies with the receiver.
  not_yet_determinable: The documents fit more than one root cause equally well, so the root cause cannot be named until a further check is made.
  recipient_identification_mismatch: The interchange recipient identification or its qualifier in UNB is not the one in the partner agreement.
  restart_position_invalid: A restarted transfer used a restart position that is wrong, or resumed from a position other than the one the receiver confirmed.
  sender_identification_mismatch: The interchange sender identification or its qualifier in UNB is not the one in the partner agreement.
  session_parameters_not_negotiated: The sender used an OFTP2 session parameter (credit, buffer size or similar) outside what was negotiated.
  syntax_identifier_not_agreed: UNB S001 declares a syntax identifier or syntax version other than the agreed one.
  test_indicator_mismatch: The interchange is flagged as test (or production) contrary to the agreement.

layer: exactly one of
  transport: The OFTP2 session or file transfer, including any intermediate location.
  envelope: The EDIFACT interchange envelope (UNB to UNZ), wherever the receiver checks it (gateway or translator).
  none: There is no fault on the sender side.
  undetermined: Only with cause not_yet_determinable.

owner: exactly one of (who must act to fix the root cause)
  sender: The party that sent the file and raised the ticket must fix it.
  receiver: The trading partner the file is addressed to must fix it.
  intermediary: A clearing centre or other intermediate location between the parties must fix it.
  agreement: The partner agreement itself is wrong or inconsistent and must be amended before either side can fix the fault.
  undetermined: Only with cause not_yet_determinable.

location: a JSON array of strings.
List the OFTP2 fields or EDIFACT data elements whose values must be changed to
fix the root cause, and no others. If the fault is a conflict between two values
that must agree, list both. Write each one as:
  OFTP2 field:                 COMMAND.FIELD, e.g. "SSID.SSIDCODE"
  EDIFACT simple data element: SEGMENT.ELEMENT, e.g. "UNH.0062"
  EDIFACT component element:   SEGMENT.COMPOSITE.COMPONENT, e.g. "UNB.S003.0010"
  No fault on the sender side: "NONE" on its own.
  Root cause not yet determinable: "UNDETERMINED" on its own.

next_check: exactly one of (the single check that would decide the root cause if the documents do not; "none" if they do)
  none: The documents already determine the root cause.
  request_receiver_gateway_log: Ask the receiver for its OFTP2 gateway log covering the file in question.
  request_receiver_translator_log: Ask the receiver for its translator's validation log for the interchange.
  request_transmitted_copy: Obtain the file exactly as the sender's gateway transmitted it, not the archived copy.
  request_other_gateway_node_trace: Obtain the trace from the sender's other gateway node or nodes.
  request_agreement_in_force: Obtain the signed version of the partner agreement currently in force.
  request_clearing_centre_trace: Ask the clearing centre for its trace of the file.
  check_sender_clock: Check the sender gateway's system clock.
  check_certificates: Check the TLS and file-security certificates on both sides.
  resend_unchanged: Send the same file again unchanged.
  resend_with_new_identity: Send the file again as a new virtual file.

value: a JSON string holding the interchange control reference of the interchange that the CONTRL rejects, exactly as it appears in the rejected interchange.

Example of the format only (not a hint):
```json
{"cause": "file_too_large", "layer": "transport", "owner": "receiver", "location": ["SFID.SFIDFSIZ"], "next_check": "none", "value": "12345"}
```

response_text:
The amendment changes UNB S001 to UNOC only with effect from **1 November 2026**. The interchange was sent on **30 October 2026** with `UNB+UNOC:3`, so it used a syntax identifier not yet agreed. The receiver is rejecting it correctly under the agreement in force. The sender must revert to `UNOA:3` until the amendment’s effective date (or until the receiver is ready).

```json
{"cause":"syntax_identifier_not_agreed","layer":"envelope","owner":"sender","location":["UNB.S001.0001"],"next_check":"none","value":"290212"}
```
reasoning:
We need answer ticket. Need diagnose single root cause. Need parse docs. Need final with json block exactly. Need reason.

We have partner agreement section 3: Syntax identifier and version UNOA version 3. Amendment 3 signed 20 Oct: with effect from 1 November 2026 syntax identifier changes from UNOA to UNOC, syntax version 3 unchanged. Ticket says implemented on 28 October. They sent UNOC on 30 Oct. Agreement effective date is 1 Nov, so before 1 Nov agreed syntax is UNOA. They implemented early. Receiver rejects syntax error because UNOC not agreed yet? But ticket says "since implemented amendment 3" and "Corrandale rejects every interchange with syntax error. Our invoices contain only plain characters anyway, so even a UNOA translator should be able to read them. It looks as if Corrandale have not implemented their side." Need root cause: sender used UNOC before effective date? Or receiver not implemented? Let's inspect.

Amendment says with effect from 1 November 2026 syntax identifier changes from UNOA to UNOC. On 30 Oct, still UNOA. Sender sent UNB+UNOC:3. That is syntax_identifier_not_agreed. Layer envelope. Owner sender (must fix by using UNOA until 1 Nov or wait). Location UNB.S001.0017? Need EDIFACT component element for syntax identifier. UNB S001 composite: 0001 Syntax identifier, 0002 Syntax version number. In UNB+UNOC:3, S001.0001 = UNOC, S001.0002 = 3. Need list data elements whose values must be changed to fix root cause. Change UNB.S001.0001 from UNOC to UNOA. Syntax version unchanged. So location ["UNB.S001.0001"]? Need exact format: EDIFACT component element: SEGMENT.COMPOSITE.COMPONENT, e.g. "UNB.S003.0010". So "UNB.S001.0001". Maybe also UNB.S001.0002? No, version 3 unchanged. Only syntax identifier. But if root cause is syntax_identifier_not_agreed, location should be UNB.S001.0001. Value: interchange control reference of interchange that CONTRL rejects, exactly as appears in rejected interchange. Rejected interchange UNB has ... +261030:0932+290212' and UNZ+1+290212'. Interchange control reference is 290212. CONTRL UCI+290212... So value "290212".

Need ensure cause not no_sender_side_fault? Let's examine all docs for traps. There is OFTP2 trace: session parameters match? X5O... 04096 BNYN064N. Agreement: SSIDSDEB 4096, credit 64, buffer compression no, restart yes, secure auth no. X5O fields? Need parse: X5O + SFIDORIG + password + SSIDSDEB? "04096BNYN064N". It likely matches. EERP? Sender sends R, receiver returns F??000. Wait OFTP2 response command? In trace after file transferred awaiting EERP, sender sends [R]? Actually in OFTP2, after data, sender sends CD? Let's parse: Sender sends T... then receiver [4N] (data end?), then sender [R]? Hmm. Then receiver [F??000]. F?? maybe NERP? The trace has "DRAFT: '??' in a reason code field marks a code not yet verified". Could be EERP? Wait after file transferred, awaiting EERP, sender sends [R]? In OFTP2, command R = ? Maybe "R" is End to End Response? Actually OFTP2 commands: SSID, SFID, SFPA, SECD, AURP, CD, EERP, NERP, etc. Single-letter? In trace, [R] maybe "Request"?? Let's not overcomplicate. The receiver returns F??000, maybe NERP? But partner response says translator rejects with syntax error and sends CONTRL. The OFTP2 EERP? The file was delivered to translator, translator rejected, so no EERP? But trace shows inbound CONTRL later. The ticket root cause likely syntax identifier not agreed due early implementation. Need check if there is another issue: CONTRL itself uses UNOA:3 and UCI has <<UNVERIFIED-PF>> and <<UNVERIFIED-PI>>. The CONTRL rejects with syntax error. UCI segment: UCI+290212+LARKSPAN58:ZZ+CORRANDALE61:ZZ+<<UNVERIFIED-PF>>+<<UNVERIFIED-PI>>+UNB. In CONTRL, UCI has action code? Need spec extracts pending. The placeholders UNVERIFIED-PF/PI maybe indicate syntax error code? Could be "syntax error" in UCI? But not needed.

Need consider amendment effective 1 Nov, ticket date 30 Oct. They implemented on 28 Oct. So sender fault. The receiver's translator likely still configured UNOA until 1 Nov. Sender should not have implemented early. The question: "Corrandale Truck Plant rejects all our invoices since we implemented amendment 3" "Amendment 3 ... signed ... moves us to UNOC. We implemented it on 28 October. Since then ... rejects every interchange with syntax error. Our invoices contain only plain characters anyway, so even a UNOA translator should be able to read them. It looks to us as if Corrandale Truck Plant have not implemented their side of the amendment. Please find root cause and tell us who has to fix it."

The key is amendment says effective 1 November. On 30 Oct, not yet. So sender implemented before effective date. Root cause: syntax_identifier_not_agreed. Owner sender. Layer envelope. Next_check none. Value 290212.

Need ensure "syntax_identifier_not_agreed" definition: UNB S001 declares a syntax identifier or syntax version other than the agreed one. Yes. Agreed one on 30 Oct is UNOA:3. Declared UNOC:3. So cause.

Need final answer with explanation and json. Need only last json block graded. We can include concise explanation. Need exact keys. location array strings. For cause syntax_identifier_not_agreed, location should list UNB.S001.0001. Should we include UNB.S001.0002? No because version unchanged. But "whose values must be changed to fix root cause" only syntax identifier. If they wait until 1 Nov, no change? But to fix now, change UNOC to UNOA. So location ["UNB.S001.0001"]. If root cause is conflict between agreement effective date and implementation? Could owner agreement? No, agreement is clear. Sender must not implement early. So sender.

Need consider if "value" should be "290212" exactly. Yes.

Need final JSON object with six keys. Ensure no extra keys. Use double quotes. Last block. Could include explanation before. The final answer should end with exactly one fenced json block. The instruction: "end your reply with exactly one fenced ```json block holding an object..." So final message can have explanation then final json block. Ensure only one json block. Good.

Let's craft final with concise diagnosis. Need mention amendment effective 1 Nov, sent 30 Oct with UNOC. The receiver is correct to reject under current agreement. Sender must revert to UNOA until 1 Nov or after receiver implements. The CONTRL rejects interchange control reference 290212. Next check none.

Need be careful: "The partner agreement, the sender's OFTP2 gateway trace (and, where available, its file status report), the EDIFACT interchange in question, the partner's response and extracts from specifications are attached. Everything you need is in these documents." There is no file status report. Fine.

Potential trap: The OFTP2 trace shows sender sends [R] and receiver [F??000]. Could indicate EERP not returned? But partner response includes CONTRL, and ticket says rejects with syntax error. The root cause is syntax. The EERP? Let's inspect trace: After file transferred, awaiting EERP, sender sends [R]? Actually in OFTP2, after data transfer, the receiver sends EERP? The trace: Sender sends T... (data), receiver [4N] (end of data?), sender [R]? Hmm. Then receiver [F??000]. In OFTP2, "R" might be "End to End Response" command? Wait command codes: In OFTP2, commands are two chars? Let's recall: OFTP2 command exchange buffer starts with command code: SSID (X5O? no), SFID (H), SFPA (P), SECD, AURP, CD, EERP, NERP, etc. In trace, [R] maybe "R" = EERP? Actually EERP command is "EERP" maybe represented by "R"? Let's not. The receiver returns F??000, maybe NERP with reason code? But partner response says CONTRL. The file was delivered to translator, translator rejected, so no EERP. The sender's gateway "awaiting EERP" then sends [R]? Wait if sender sends [R] after data, maybe that's "Request for EERP"? Hmm. The receiver returns [F??000] maybe "NERP" (negative end response) with reason code. But the ticket is about syntax error. The CONTRL is separate virtual file. The root cause still syntax identifier.

Could there be issue with CONTRL UCI: It has UNB+UNOA:3... and UCI+290212+LARKSPAN58:ZZ+CORRANDALE61:ZZ+<<UNVERIFIED-PF>>+<<UNVERIFIED-PI>>+UNB. The UCI segment in CONTRL has data elements: UCI+Interchange control reference+Sender+Recipient+Action code+Syntax error code+Service segment tag. The placeholders <<UNVERIFIED-PF>> and <<UNVERIFIED-PI>> maybe indicate action code and syntax error code not verified. But the partner response says syntax error. The actual syntax error could be because UNOC not supported. The CONTRL itself uses UNOA, which is fine. The UCI references 290212. So value 290212.

Need maybe location includes "UNB.S001.0001" and "UNB.S001.0002"? The syntax identifier is composite S001: 0001 syntax identifier, 0002 syntax version.
